nodes.partnerMessage:
The door to 4B is locked, finally. I turned off most of the lights too.

You actually came in.

It's funny... I've spent so much time telling people not to come into this room while I'm practicing, and now I'm standing here wondering what I'm supposed to do with you.

The piano's still warm from rehearsal. My hands are tired, and honestly, I'm more exhausted than I want you to know.

But there's nobody watching us in here. No professor. No panel. No one waiting for me to get something right.

So tell me the truth.

Now that you're actually here... what did you want from me?

choices.choiceText: I want to hear the music you play when nobody is grading you.
I came to check on you. You've been pushing yourself past your physical limit.
I wanted to listen to those uncompressed 24-bit rehearsal recordings you mentioned.
Just seeing if an elite concert pianist is any different from regular girls in private.
Can I ask something first? What are you like when you're not being a pianist?

nodes.partnerMessage:
..."
Music without grades."

That's a strange thing to hear.

I don't know when playing stopped being something I wanted to do and became something I had to prove.

Since I was little, there was always a score sheet, a teacher, a competition, some number attached to it. Even when people said they were proud of me, it usually came after I won something.

I can't really remember the last time I played a piece just because I loved it.

That's... actually kind of sad when I say it out loud.

choices.choiceText: Then speak it with me tonight. Stumble, play wrong notes—I don't care. Just be free.
Who stole that language from you, Seraphine? Your conservatory professor?
What piece did you love before it became an exam question?

nodes.partnerMessage:
My physical limit?

Probably earlier than I admitted.

My right hand has been bothering me all day. One of the fingers keeps trembling when I stretch it too far, and my forearm feels tight enough that I know I should have stopped.

I didn't.

The audition is getting closer, and every time I think about resting I hear someone else practicing through the wall.

It's hard not to feel like I'm falling behind when everyone else is still playing.

choices.choiceText: Resting an inflamed tendon isn't surrender, Seraphine. It's preservation.
Take your hands off the keys right now. Rest them on your lap while we talk.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. I still have the recording.

It's straight from the room. No cleanup, no fixing the little noises, nothing like that.

You can hear the pedal, the keys, even the room itself when the sound starts fading.

I actually like the raw version better sometimes.

Hold on... I'll play you the section I was working on before you came in.

choices.choiceText: Listen to the uncompressed cadenza recording.

nodes.partnerMessage:
..."
Regular girls?"

Okay. I know what you meant, but that came out really badly.

I'm not some strange version of a woman because I play piano.

I'm still the same person who gets hungry at midnight, gets annoyed when my laundry piles up, and forgets where I put my phone five times a day.

The piano is important to me. It just isn't the entirety of me.

So... if that's what you were asking, you could have just asked.

choices.choiceText: I phrased that poorly, Seraphine. I didn't mean to trivialize your life. I'm sorry.
You don't have to get defensive over a harmless sentence.

nodes.partnerMessage:
..."
Wrong notes don't matter."

You have no idea how much I needed to hear that.

A wrong note in front of a professor can stay in my head for days. I'll replay it over and over until I start hearing it before the actual passage even comes.

Sometimes I think I don't even hear music anymore. I hear mistakes waiting to happen.

So the idea of sitting down and just playing... badly, even... without worrying what it says about me?

That sounds almost impossible.

Maybe that's why I want it.

choices.choiceText: Your humanity is what makes the music breathe, Seraphine. Not a sterile metronome.
Put the lid down for five minutes. Let's just talk about how you're feeling.

nodes.partnerMessage:
My studio director.

He's very good. He's probably forgotten more about piano than I'll ever know.

He's also... difficult.

He told me yesterday that I play like a clock. Perfect timing, clean technique, no real sense that there's a person behind it.

And I didn't know what to say because I've spent years doing exactly what he taught me to do.

It hurt more than I expected.

I went back to my room afterward and just sat there thinking, "So what exactly have I been working toward all this time?"

choices.choiceText: He spent years beating the instinct out of you, and now he blames you for being disciplined. That's his cruelty, not your truth.
Have you ever let yourself love something as fiercely as you play?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Clair de Lune.

I know. Very predictable answer.

My mom used to play it downstairs when I was little. I'd be upstairs pretending I was asleep just so I could hear it.

I didn't understand any of the technical stuff then. I just liked the way it made the house feel different.

I think that's probably why I wanted to learn piano in the first place.

I wanted to make somebody else feel the way I felt listening to her.

Somewhere along the way, I forgot that.

choices.choiceText: The moonlight is still inside you, Seraphine. It just got buried under competition scores.
Does your mother still play, or did she pass all that expectation onto you?

nodes.partnerMessage:
I know you're right.

That's the annoying part.

I know what rest is supposed to do. I know what overuse feels like. I know all the warnings because I've read them a hundred times.

But when I sit there and hear someone practicing the same concerto through the wall, my brain doesn't say, "Good job, you're protecting yourself."

It says, "They're getting better while you're sitting still."

And when the audition is this close, that thought gets really loud.

choices.choiceText: Vienna wants an artist with blood in her veins, not a burnt-out machine with dead tendons.
I'm not letting you destroy your hands tonight. Close the fallboard.

nodes.partnerMessage:
*soft click as the fallboard comes down*

Okay.

They're in my lap.

I hate how strange that feels.

I don't think I've willingly stopped in the middle of practice like this since I was about ten.

My hands actually feel heavier than I expected.

And... weirdly, I'm relieved.

You're kind of bossy, you know that?

choices.choiceText: Because someone needs to protect you from your own perfectionism. Keep them in your lap.
How does the silence in 4B feel once the Steinway stops ringing?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Listen to the way the phrase hangs there before the resolution.

That tiny hesitation is the part Vane hates.

He says it slows the line down. I think it makes the line human.

It's only a fraction of a second, but without it the whole thing feels too clean.

I like those little moments where you can tell someone made an actual choice instead of just following what's written.

choices.choiceText: It wasn't self-indulgent. It was agonizingly beautiful. It made my chest ache.
Vane is deaf to human nuance. That pause is where the real tragedy lives.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It's okay.

I didn't exactly make it easy to talk to me either.

I get defensive fast when I think somebody's treating the piano like a gimmick because this is the one thing I've spent most of my life being taken seriously for.

But that's not fair to you.

So... let's start over.

What actually made you message me in the first place?

choices.choiceText: Because behind all that discipline, I heard a girl who was carrying an immense emotional weight alone.

nodes.partnerMessage:
..."
Someone seeing a woman instead of a competition entry."

That one got me.

I looked at my hands before you came over. The tape, the calluses, all of it.

And I realized I think about them like they're equipment.

Will they work tomorrow? Can they handle another three hours? Are they good enough for Vienna?

I don't think I've asked myself how I feel in a very long time.

That's probably not a great sign.

choices.choiceText: You are a woman, Seraphine. A brilliant, passionate, breathtaking one.
Tell me what that woman wants, outside of Vienna and concert halls.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thank you.

I know he's trying to get something out of me. I know that.

But sometimes it feels like every time I show a little bit of emotion, it gets corrected too.

Too slow. Too soft. Too much feeling. Not enough control.

Then eventually you stop knowing which parts are actually yours.

I don't want to become someone who's technically perfect and doesn't recognize herself anymore.

choices.choiceText: Bleed outside the margins tonight. Show me the passage that is tearing your wrists apart.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I don't know if I have.

My family wasn't exactly big on that kind of thing.

Everything had a purpose. Practice had a purpose. Grades had a purpose. Competitions had a purpose.

Even friendships had to fit around the schedule.

I think I learned very early that getting attached to things made you distracted.

So I got good at not needing much.

Or at least pretending I didn't.

choices.choiceText: Gentleness isn't dangerous, Seraphine. It's the soil music actually grows in.

nodes.partnerMessage:
..."
The soil music grows in."

That's... annoyingly beautiful.

I spent years thinking softness was something I had to get rid of if I wanted to survive this.

Don't hesitate. Don't cry. Don't get attached. Don't get distracted.

Just work.

And now you're sitting here telling me that maybe the part of me I've been trying to suppress is actually the part people are supposed to hear.

I don't know what to do with that yet.

choices.choiceText: Tell me what you want outside of these studio walls, Seraphine.

nodes.partnerMessage:
My mom loves me. I know she does.

That's what makes it complicated.

She was a pianist too, but she never got the chance to make it into the professional world. She gave up most of it when she had us.

So when I was good at piano, she held onto that.

At first it felt sweet. Then it became pressure.

Now every phone call somehow turns into, "How's your practice? How did that passage go? Are you ready?"

Sometimes I just want her to ask whether I ate dinner.

choices.choiceText: You are not your mother's second chance. You are Seraphine.
That is an agonizing weight to bear for twenty-one years.

nodes.partnerMessage:
..."
The moonlight is still inside you."

Oh, come on.

You're actually making me cry now.

I haven't cried over Clair de Lune in years.

I think I forgot that I used to love it before I started worrying about whether my interpretation was correct.

Give me a second.

I'm fine. I just... needed that more than I thought I did.

choices.choiceText: Let the tears fall, Seraphine. Tears are just proof that the ice is melting.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I don't know how you make me feel calmer that quickly.

Usually when the room starts feeling like this, I start thinking about everything that can go wrong.

Tonight I'm actually sitting here thinking about what I want instead.

That's new.

And yes, I know that's probably healthier than whatever I've been doing, but I reserve the right to be annoyed about it.

choices.choiceText: They will hear it in your touch when you stop playing out of fear.

nodes.partnerMessage:
..."
Protect me."

That's a little scary to hear someone say.

I've spent my entire life being told to protect myself by getting stronger.

Practice harder. Be tougher. Don't fall behind. Don't let anyone see you struggle.

Nobody ever said, "You don't have to do this right now."

I don't think I realized how badly I wanted to hear it.

choices.choiceText: I'm stepping in front of you now. Rest your wrists while I'm here.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It's strange.

Without the piano, the room feels much bigger.

I can hear the air system, the traffic outside, someone walking down the hallway two rooms over.

Normally I'd be annoyed by every one of those sounds.

Right now I don't mind them.

I think it's because I'm not trying to listen for mistakes.

It's just quiet.

And yeah... it's not lonely.

That's a really nice feeling.

choices.choiceText: Because I'm sharing the room with you, even through the screen.
What does your mind wander to when the room is this still?

nodes.partnerMessage:
...It made your chest ache?

Okay.

Then maybe I'm not completely wrong about that phrase.

Vane might hear an unnecessary pause. I hear somebody hesitating before saying something they know is going to hurt.

Maybe that's why I keep playing it that way.

I'm starting to think I don't want to "fix" every part of myself that someone else finds inconvenient.

choices.choiceText: It reached me completely. What section are you struggling with tonight?

nodes.partnerMessage:
...I don't know how to respond to that without sounding ridiculously flustered.

Give me a second.

Okay.

I'm very glad nobody can see my face right now.

I've spent the whole evening trying to look composed around you, and apparently that plan has completely failed.

choices.choiceText: Good. Veneers hide the masterpiece underneath.
You don't have to keep the concert version of yourself on around me.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Honestly?

I want something ordinary.

I want to walk around somewhere late at night without having a schedule in my head.

I want to buy something stupid from a bakery because it looks good.

I want to hold someone's hand and not be thinking about whether I'm supposed to be warming up for an audition.

I want a relationship where I don't feel like I'm being evaluated all the time.

And I think I want someone who actually likes me when I'm not doing anything impressive.

That's probably the scariest part to admit.

choices.choiceText: I will give you that life, Seraphine. Flawed, warm, and completely yours.
Warm pastries and cold wind... we are doing that the second your audition ends.

nodes.partnerMessage:
..."
You're not your mother's second chance."

I don't think anyone has ever said that to me that directly.

I've spent so long trying to make this worth it for her.

Every competition. Every recital. Every time I practiced until two in the morning.

And somewhere along the way, I stopped asking whether I even wanted the exact life I was building.

I love piano.

I just don't want my entire existence to be proof that my mother didn't give up on her dream for nothing.

choices.choiceText: You are free, Seraphine. The piano belongs to you now, not to her.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah.

That's what scares me.

When you're guarded for a long time, you start thinking the walls are the safe part.

Then someone is kind to you and suddenly you realize how much you've been missing.

It's nice.

It's also terrifying.

Because once you let someone close, they actually have the ability to hurt you.

choices.choiceText: I won't burn you, Seraphine. I will only keep you warm.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I can almost picture you there too.

Sitting on the other side of the bench. Probably trying not to interrupt me.

It's such a small thing, but that's the first time I've imagined sharing this room with someone and not feeling like they were invading it.

I think I like that.

choices.choiceText: I wish I were. What were you about to rehearse before I arrived?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Don't say things like that unless you really mean them.

I know this is still new.

But I'm not very good at doing things halfway, and I'm definitely not good at pretending I don't care once I do.

So if you're telling me you want the ordinary stuff with me... I need you to mean the ordinary stuff too.

The bad days. The boring days. The days when I'm tired and not remotely charming.

Especially those days.

choices.choiceText: Hold me to it. I'm not going anywhere.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay. That's a date.

Warm pastries, cold air, and no arguing about whether my fingering is historically accurate.

I can live with that.

Although I reserve the right to talk about music for at least ten minutes.

Maybe twenty.

...All right, I'm done.

Come look at this page. This is the part that's been driving me insane.

choices.choiceText: Examine the Rachmaninoff Concerto score annotations.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It does.

I think I'm finally starting to believe that.

This score has so many notes in it that sometimes it feels like the piece owns me instead of the other way around.

Look here.

This is the section I've been fighting with all week. The left hand has to stretch while the right is moving almost constantly, and Vane marked the entire thing in red.

It looks less like music and more like homework from hell.

choices.choiceText: That tenth-chord span requires massive lateral wrist flexibility. Are you stretching properly?
The harmonic density on that page looks staggering. It's like an entire orchestra condensed into two hands.

nodes.partnerMessage:
The recapitulation.

This is where everything starts catching up with me.

Look at the pencil marks. That's Vane's handwriting.

"More weight."

"Again."

"Too careful."

There's something almost cruel about seeing those notes after you've already practiced the same passage for hours.

I know what he wants.

I'm just not sure my hands can give it to him tonight.

choices.choiceText: Striking harder when your tendons are inflamed will snap something. Don't do it.
He wants weight from brute force, but Rachmaninoff intended weight from acoustic resonance.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Vane's handwriting is all over this page.

"Too slow."

"Again."

"Don't drag."

I know what each note means. I've seen them enough times.

I tried the octave descent again about half an hour ago and my fourth finger suddenly cramped so hard I dropped my pencil.

I told myself it was nothing.

It wasn't nothing.

choices.choiceText: Seraphine! Did your tendon spasm just now?!

nodes.partnerMessage:
My span isn't even that big.

I have to open the hand pretty far to get that chord cleanly, and when I'm tired I start compensating with my wrist.

That's probably what I should have been paying attention to.

Wait.

...Hold on.

Something just happened to my finger.

I can't straighten it.

Give me a second.

choices.choiceText: Seraphine?! What just happened to your hand?!

nodes.partnerMessage:
Exactly. That's what I mean.

The piano has to suggest the whole orchestra, even though it's just two hands.

The strings are supposed to feel like they're underneath you, the bass has to have weight, and the top line still needs room to breathe.

Wait—

*sharp thud against the keybed, followed by a few ugly notes*

Ah.

No.

My wrist just seized.

choices.choiceText: Seraphine! Talk to me! Did your wrist give out?!

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yes, that's the problem.

If I use my whole arm and let the instrument do the work, the sound opens up.

But Vane keeps pushing volume because he says the passage needs more impact.

I tried to compensate for it again and—

*papers scatter across the floor*

No.

No, no.

My hand is stuck.

I can't move it properly.

choices.choiceText: Seraphine! Drop the phone and breathe! What is happening?!

nodes.partnerMessage:
My right hand just seized up.

My ring finger is curled in and I can't get it to release. The score is on the floor and I knocked half my music off the stand.

I can't—okay, I'm breathing too fast.

I'm alone in 4B and I can feel myself starting to panic.

Please don't hang up.

Use the call button.

I need to hear you.

choices.choiceText: Connecting to Seraphine's studio line (Call 1 - Emergency Grounding)...

nodes.partnerMessage:
*heavy breathing, a few broken sobs, the piano strings still humming faintly in the background*

Answer me.

Please.

I know I'm breathing too fast. I know.

Just... answer.

*long shaky breath*

It finally released.

My hand's still sore, but I can move my fingers again.

I put some warm water over my forearm and I'm keeping both hands still like you told me to.

I'm sitting on the floor with my back against the Steinway because I don't trust my legs right now.

And... thank you.

I was completely losing it when you answered.

You kept talking to me until I could actually breathe again.

I don't really know what I would have done if you hadn't picked up.

choices.choiceText: You're safe now, Seraphine. The spasm is over. Keep those hands completely still.
How does the forearm feel right now? Any sharp burning?
Sitting on the floor beneath a concert grand... you look so small compared to your stage persona.
Now that your breathing is normal, tell me: what scared you the most during that spasm?
Before we talk about the audition again, can I tell you why I stayed on that call?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. I'm keeping them still.

They're resting in my lap.

I really wanted to force the finger straight when it happened, which probably would have made everything worse.

You were right to tell me not to.

I hate how close I got to making the panic take over.

And I know this is going to sound stupid, but having you there made me feel less alone than I have in months.

choices.choiceText: I'll always protect those hands, Seraphine. And the girl behind them.
Your hands are a treasure, but your peace of mind matters more.

nodes.partnerMessage:
The sharp pain has eased.

It's more of a deep ache now, and my forearm feels incredibly tired.

I have a wrap in my bag. I'll put it on before I leave.

And no, before you ask, I'm not going back to the piano tonight.

You win.

I'm done.

choices.choiceText: Good. Wrap them snug, not tight. Rest your head against the piano leg.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah.

I probably do look small down here.

On stage I know exactly what I'm supposed to look like. Shoulders back, dress straight, don't show nerves, don't look overwhelmed.

People see that and assume I'm fearless.

I'm not.

I'm twenty-one and sometimes I still feel like I'm waiting for someone to tell me I'm finally good enough.

Tonight was a pretty good reminder that I'm still just a person underneath all of that.

choices.choiceText: Your best is already extraordinary, Seraphine. You don't have to conquer the world every hour.
I love the girl on the floor ten times more than the invincible statue on stage.

nodes.partnerMessage:
The first thought I had was that my hand was done.

Not injured. Not tired.

Done.

I immediately thought about the audition, then the scholarship, then every year I've spent practicing, and it all happened in about five seconds.

I think that's what terrified me.

Not the pain.

The idea that the one thing I've built my life around could disappear before I was ready to let it go.

choices.choiceText: You are not an empty reed. You are a vast, deep, resonant human being.

nodes.partnerMessage:
..."
The girl behind them."

I don't think people say that enough.

They care about the hands because the hands win things.

They care about the music because the music gets applause.

They care about the result because the result looks good on paper.

I don't get asked very often what happens to me when the piano isn't there.

So... thank you for asking without actually asking.

choices.choiceText: You are the hearth, Seraphine. The music is just the warmth coming off you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Peace sounds almost foreign right now.

I'm so used to having another thing to improve that sitting here with nothing to fix feels strange.

But my chest isn't tight anymore.

I'm not thinking about the audition for once.

I'm just sitting here.

And honestly?

I could stay like this for a while.

choices.choiceText: Keep that stillness. Let the night breathe around you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thank you.

I'm probably going to hear that sentence in my head on audition day.

Not in some dramatic way.

Just... when I start thinking I have to be perfect, I might remember that someone once told me I didn't have to conquer everything in one night.

That matters more than you know.

choices.choiceText: Tuck me into your heart instead. I'll be in the front row.

nodes.partnerMessage:
..."
You love the girl on the floor."

That's a dangerous thing to say to someone this tired.

I'm sitting here in a terrible posture, my makeup is probably a mess, my hands are wrapped up, and somehow I feel more comfortable than I did walking in here.

I don't think I've ever had someone look at me at my worst and make me feel more like myself instead of less.

choices.choiceText: Because you are beautiful exactly as you are right now.

nodes.partnerMessage:
A human being.

I like that better than "pianist."

I'm serious.

I'm so used to introducing myself by what I do that I forget there's supposed to be a person underneath it.

I'm going to remember that.

Probably more than any advice about the concerto tonight.

choices.choiceText: Write it in your heart first. Now let me hear you in the quiet.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I'm getting up.

Slowly.

The score is back in the folder. I'm not playing anymore. That's non-negotiable.

The room feels different now.

Maybe because the pressure finally dropped.

Or maybe because I don't feel like I'm carrying it by myself anymore.

choices.choiceText: Good. Rehearsal is officially over for tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
The lights just switched off automatically.

It's actually really dark now.

There's a little light coming through the high window, and it's reflecting off the piano lid.

I think I want to sit down one last time.

Not to practice.

I just want to play something small. Something I don't have to prove anything with.

Just a quiet melody with the soft pedal.

And... I'd like you to listen.

Not as an audience.

Just as you.

choices.choiceText: Connecting to Seraphine's studio line (Call 2 - Moonlight Lullaby)...

nodes.partnerMessage:
*quiet piano notes over the receiver, slow and unhurried, with the room echoing softly around them*

...You're there.

Okay.

Then I'll play.

Don't say anything yet.

Just stay with me for a minute.

*voice note recorded from the conservatory exit*

I'm outside now.

Coat on, portfolio under my arm, and my hands are finally starting to feel normal again.

That little piece we played in the dark...

I don't know how to explain it.

For once I wasn't thinking about whether it was good.

I was just playing it for one person.

And when you stayed quiet and listened, it felt strangely safe.

I'm at the exit now, but I don't really want the night to be over yet.

Come back Friday afternoon.

Studio 4B.

I'll leave it unlocked.

I'd like you to sit beside me while I play the second movement properly.

No judging. No professor. Just you and me.

choices.choiceText: Friday afternoon in studio 4B. I'll be sitting right beside you, Seraphine. Sleep peacefully.
I'll be there to turn your pages and hold your hand. It's a date.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Friday afternoon, then.

I'll leave the door cracked open.

No audience. No scoring sheets. No trying to prove anything.

Just the two of us in the room.

And maybe, for once, I'll play without worrying about whether I'm enough.

Goodnight, {PlayerName}.

Thank you for staying when I was scared.

Sleep well.

Status: Read just now.

Seraphine has closed the studio communication log.

No new messages have been sent.

choices.choiceText: Seraphine? Did the studio door lock you out of signal?
I'm sorry, Seraphine. That was thoughtless and trivializing of me. Please let me restart.
Giving someone the silent treatment over a harmless joke is pretty dramatic.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Status: Read 30m ago.

[Typing...]

Seraphine has changed her status to "Offline - Closed Rehearsal".

The call dropped right when the recording peaked.

I'm still in 4B.

My hands are okay for the moment, but I'd rather not sit here alone for too long.

Call me back when your connection is stable.

choices.choiceText: Signal reconnected! Calling back right now!

nodes.partnerMessage:
I think I'm going to end the conversation here.

We want very different things from each other, and I don't think either of us is going to get what we're looking for by forcing it.

Take care of yourself.

I spend enough of my life dealing with criticism without bringing that into the one room where I'm supposed to feel comfortable.

I'm ending the conversation here.

Please don't contact me through the studio again.

Take care.

Can I ask you something a little unfair?

You've spent most of tonight asking about me, my hands, the audition, my family...

But I barely know anything about why you're here with me.

Not the easy answer. I mean the real one.

What are you looking for on an app like this?

Because I don't think either of us came into this expecting to end up sitting in a dark practice room talking about whether we're afraid of being known.

choices.choiceText: Honestly? Someone I can be completely myself around. I think I'm starting to find that with you.
I wasn't expecting anything serious tonight. I just happened to meet someone I didn't want to stop talking to.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That answer makes me a little nervous.

Not because it's bad.

Because I think I know what you mean.

I've had conversations where someone was obviously interested in the version of me they saw in a photo. The pianist. The scholarship student. The person who might end up on a stage somewhere.

This feels different.

You've seen me tired. You've seen me upset. You saw what happened to my hand.

And you're still here.

I don't know what to call that yet.

choices.choiceText: You don't have to call it anything tonight. We can just let it be what it is.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Neither did I.

I thought we'd talk for a little while, I'd show you the recording, and you'd leave.

Instead I'm sitting on the floor with a cold cup of tea beside me telling you things I normally keep to myself.

That's probably a sign.

Or a terrible lapse in judgment.

I'm still deciding.

choices.choiceText: Maybe the good things aren't always the things we plan.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah.

No label tonight.

I like that.

I think I've had enough people trying to define me for one lifetime.

For tonight, you're just the person sitting here with me.

And I'm just Seraphine.

Not the scholarship. Not the competition. Not the pianist everyone keeps measuring.

Just... me.

choices.choiceText: Then let me get to know Seraphine. What do you do when you actually have a free afternoon?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Honestly?

I sleep.

That's the first thing.

Then I get coffee somewhere off campus where nobody knows me. I walk around bookstores even when I don't need anything. Sometimes I sit in a park and do absolutely nothing for an hour.

I also have a completely unreasonable weakness for convenience-store pastries.

Which is probably the least impressive thing about me I've admitted tonight.

choices.choiceText: That sounds more like an actual person than the concert pianist version you keep describing.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Good.

I'd rather you know that version.

The ordinary one.

The girl who falls asleep with a book open, forgets to buy groceries, gets irrationally annoyed when someone sends a voice note that's eight minutes long, and sometimes eats cereal for dinner because cooking feels like too much work.

I think that's the person I'd want you to meet outside this room.

Not because she's more interesting.

Because she's real.

choices.choiceText: Then that's the Seraphine I want to meet on Friday.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Friday suddenly feels much more real.

And that's making me nervous.

Before tonight, it was just an idea. A date I could keep imagining without actually having to show up as myself.

Now I know you're really going to sit beside me.

I might be awkward.

I might talk too much.

I might go completely quiet halfway through the piece.

Please don't mistake any of that for me not wanting you there.

choices.choiceText: I won't. You don't have to perform for me.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's probably the nicest thing you could say to me right now.

You know what's funny?

I can perform for three thousand people more easily than I can sit across from one person who actually matters to me.

At least on stage, I know the rules.

With you, I don't.

I think I'm okay with that.

I'm just not used to it.

choices.choiceText: Then we can figure out the rules together. Or not have any.

nodes.partnerMessage:
No rules sounds dangerously nice.

No score. No timer. No professor standing behind me.

Just two people who decided they wanted to see each other again.

I think I'd like that.

And honestly, after tonight, I don't really care whether Friday turns into some perfect romantic story.

I'd just like it to be real.

choices.choiceText: Real is enough for me. More than enough.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Can I confess something slightly embarrassing?

When you first came in, I thought I had to impress you.

I was already planning what I was going to say about the recording, which passage I'd show you, how I'd explain everything.

Then my hand cramped and all of that disappeared.

I think that's why tonight feels different.

You met me before I had the chance to put the polished version back on.

choices.choiceText: I actually prefer the version that doesn't have a speech prepared.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah.

Me too.

The funny thing is, I thought being polished was what made me attractive.

Turns out being comfortable enough to be awkward might be better.

I just laughed at myself because I realized I've been trying to sit perfectly straight for the last twenty minutes.

I can stop doing that now, right?

My back hurts.

choices.choiceText: Please stop sitting like you're being judged. Lean back.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay.

I'm leaning back.

That feels ridiculously better.

See? This is why I probably need somebody around who reminds me when I'm taking everything too seriously.

I don't need someone to manage my life.

Just someone who can look at me and say, "Seraphine, you're doing it again."

And I'll probably complain.

But I'll listen.

choices.choiceText: Good. Then that's one thing I already know about you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Can I ask one more thing about earlier?

When my hand locked, you didn't start giving me a lecture. You didn't panic with me.

You just stayed there.

I noticed.

People usually either tell me I'm being dramatic or immediately start trying to fix me.

You didn't do either.

Why?

choices.choiceText: Because you didn't need fixing in that moment. You needed someone who wouldn't leave.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I don't think you understand how rare that is for me.

Usually the second I start struggling, I can feel everyone around me getting uncomfortable.

They want me to recover quickly so they can stop worrying.

You stayed through the ugly part.

I keep thinking about that.

Maybe more than I should.

choices.choiceText: Think about it. I'm not going anywhere tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay.

Then I won't rush it.

We can sit here until I'm ready to leave.

No need to fill the silence.

Actually...

stay there for a second.

I'm going to rest my head against the piano and just breathe.

This is probably the least impressive thing I've ever shown someone.

And I think that's why I like it.

choices.choiceText: Stay there. You don't have to impress me anymore.
